risks.description: Delay in developing the internal CRM minimum-viable product by November 2025 could impair the expression of interest process for Cohort 1 schools.
risks.mitigation: Prioritize core functional requirements for the MVP release by November 2025 and establish manual backup processes for school engagement.
risks.evidence: develop a customer relationship management system internally, working towards a minimum-viable product from November 2025.

risks.description: Transition of existing National School Breakfast Programme schools may result in delivery gaps when NSBP closes in July 2026 before September 2026 FBC launch.
risks.mitigation: Guarantee places for all 1,700+ participating NSBP schools and issue invitations early to ensure seamless onboarding.
risks.evidence: ensure they do not have a gap in provision after the closure of the NSBP in July 2026.

risks.description: Primary schools may experience physical space and estate constraints preventing effective delivery of breakfast clubs for all enrolled pupils.
risks.mitigation: Deploy technical estate advisers to evaluate spatial limitations and assist affected schools with space mitigation solutions.
risks.evidence: continuing contracts of technical estate advisers to test what schools can do to mitigate any space constraints.

risks.description: Uncertainty in daily turnout and operational costs at individual school levels may create funding deficits or unexpected cost variances.
risks.mitigation: Provide £1,000 initial set-up grants combined with standard daily fixed (£25) and variable per-pupil funding allocations.
risks.evidence: evidence-based, but there will always be a level of uncertainty at an individual school level and on a day-to-day basis.

risks.description: Delays or withholding of timely budget approval and confirmation from HM Treasury could disrupt ongoing rollout and expansion.
risks.mitigation: Maintain rigorous analytical modelling, present evidence from early adopters, and engage early with HM Treasury via project board governance.
risks.evidence: The programme's success depends on several factors. These include timely approval and budget confirmation from HM Treasury

risks.description: Shortages in skilled personnel within DfE or participating schools could impede program execution and club supervision.
risks.mitigation: Procure external specialist support advisers through established commercial frameworks and pilot call-centre operational assistance.
risks.evidence: availability of skilled staff and resources, in both DfE and the education sector.

risks.description: Delays in passing or enacting the Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill could undermine the statutory foundation for mandatory school delivery.
risks.mitigation: Drive voluntary engagement through grant incentives and phased onboarding ahead of statutory duty commencement.
risks.evidence: Children's Wellbeing and Schools Bill will place a duty on state-funded schools with primary-aged children

risks.description: Upfront Year 1 operational expenditures incurred before attainment benefits accrue after one year could undermine early cost-benefit metrics.
risks.mitigation: Track and highlight immediate short-term benefits, such as childcare savings and parental workforce participation, alongside longer-term attainment data.
risks.evidence: costs are incurred upfront while attainment benefits only materialise after at least one year.

risks.description: Historical funding complexity based on disadvantage levels may confuse mainstream school leaders and decrease willingness to participate.
risks.mitigation: Implement a simplified, predictable funding model with flat daily rates and clear per-pupil allocations.
risks.evidence: variation by disadvantage levels was deemed to be complicated for mainstream schools, resulting in confusion.

risks.description: Onboarding approximately 2,000 schools across two cohorts within Year 1 may exceed program administrative and operational capacity.
risks.mitigation: Deploy a hybrid delivery model combining internal DfE capacity with external specialist advisers and funded local authority support.
risks.evidence: combining in-house capability with contracted specialist support to assist onboarding of around 2,000 schools over 2 cohorts.

risks.description: Lack of alignment with broader government programs or local authority initiatives could lead to operational friction and fragmented service delivery.
risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated funding to local authorities to support system integration and maintain multi-layered governance across government missions.
risks.evidence: The programme's success depends on several factors... alignment with other government programmes
